title: Multi-joint upper-limb MI dataset from Yi et al. 2025
description: This dataset contains 62-channel EEG recordings from 18 healthy, right-handed participants performing motor imagery of eight multi-joint movements of the unilateral upper limb. The movements involve the hand, wrist, elbow and shoulder. Each participant completed 320 cue-based trials across 8 blocks, with 40 trials per class. The data support research on brain-computer interfaces for motor rehabilitation.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Neuroscan SynAmps2 amplifier at 1000 Hz from 62 channels, referenced to the left mastoid (M1). Participants were cued by video and text and imagined each movement for 4 s. The eight classes were hand open/close, wrist flexion/extension, wrist abduction/adduction, elbow pronation/supination, elbow flexion/extension, shoulder pronation/supination, shoulder abduction/adduction, and shoulder flexion/extension. Each participant completed one session of 8 blocks with 40 trials per block (5 per class).
